govdocs-archive_org-nsia-AutopsyJFKHelpe: Material on the Kennedy autopsy filed under the names Helpern and Houts makes up this document. Dr. Milton Helpern, New York's chief medical examiner, was the most prominent pathologist to criticize the official autopsy from outside it, and his name runs through the medical debate on the case. The file is kept as issued, part of the paper record of the long argument over the autopsy evidence.

K is a novel by Mary Roberts Rinehart. It opens on a quiet street of ancient houses that seemed to meet in the distance. A man under thirty, worn by long wandering, finds the street infinitely inviting. He hopes for peace there: long evenings to read, quiet nights to sleep and forget. The little house asks him for no references, to his surprise.

Across the street, Joe Drummond waits under a lamp for a girl who keeps him hanging about. Prayer meeting is over, and the young people are pairing off along the curb. Joe swears he will fool her this once and leave her to worry. Rinehart sets her story of the man called K inside this small street of courtship, secrets, and watched windows.
